# CLI Evidence: Help

### abx --help

```
$ abx --help
Usage: abx [options] [command]

abx — Agent Sandbox CLI

Deploy useful templates and manage their running instances.

Get started:
  abx config init
  abx deploy python-hello --name demo
  abx status demo
  abx delete demo

Author templates:
  abx template list python
  abx template init ./my-template --from python-hello
  abx deploy ./my-template --name demo

Use --json for machine-readable output. --yes separately authorizes changes.
More templates: https://registry.agent-sandbox.cn/templates/

Options:
  --version            Show the version and exit.
  -j, --json           Machine-readable JSON output
  -q, --quiet          Minimal output
  -v, --verbose        Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  --no-color           Disable colored output
  --log-level <LEVEL>  Set log level explicitly (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
  --ci                 Machine-readable CI/CD output; does not authorize changes
  -h, --help           Show this message and exit.

Command groups:
  template             Discover, create, build and publish reusable templates.
  config               Configure credentials, Providers and defaults.
  provider             Install Providers and inspect or run native operations.
  mcp                  Configure and run the local MCP server.

Commands:
  sandbox              Inspect and invoke a Sandbox's registered API operations.
  deploy               Deploy a template as a named instance.
  list                 List deployments and Sandboxes.
  status               Inspect a deployment or Sandbox ID.
  logs                 Read deployment or Sandbox logs.
  delete               Delete a deployment or Sandbox ID.
  recover              Inspect and recover an interrupted deployment.
  exec                 Execute a program in a Sandbox.
  connect              Connect to a Sandbox terminal.
  upload               Upload a local file to a Sandbox.
  download             Download a file from a Sandbox.
  capabilities         Inspect a Sandbox's available runtime capabilities.
  files                Read and manage Sandbox files.
  process              Inspect and control Sandbox processes.
  system               Inspect the Sandbox runtime environment.
  pause                Pause a Sandbox while retaining its state.
  resume               Resume a paused Sandbox.
  metrics              Read Sandbox resource metrics.
  snapshot             Create, list and delete Sandbox snapshots.
  fork                 Fork a running Sandbox.
  network              Read or update a Sandbox's network policy.

Provider: alicloud-express (default)
36 provider operations: api-key, quota, sandbox, snapshot, team, template-cache, template, volume.
Example: abx provider run api-key.create --help
Use 'abx provider --help' for the directory and 'abx provider run OPERATION --help' for parameters.
Select for one invocation: abx --provider ID provider --help
Exit code: 0
```

### config --help

```
$ abx config --help
Usage: abx config [options] [command]

Manage persistent credentials and CLI defaults.

Values are read from ~/.abx/config.toml and ~/.abx/.env. Environment
variables can still override the stored configuration at runtime.

Examples:
  abx config init
  abx config list
  abx config get region
  abx config set http_timeout 120
  abx config set github_token     Prompt for the token (masked input)
  abx config delete region   Remove one stored value

Related commands:
  abx config init           Guided setup (credentials, region, ACR, LLM)
  abx config get            Read one effective value
  abx config set            Store or update one value
  abx config delete KEY     Remove one stored value

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  delete      Remove one stored configuration value.
  get         Get a configuration value by KEY.
  init        Guided setup with optional template search and launch (add --build
              / --llm for focused setup).
  list        List all effective configuration values and their sources.
  set         Set a configuration value: KEY [VALUE].
Exit code: 0
```

  abx provider run api-key.reset  [write]  Rotate an API key and save its new secret exclusively to secret_file.
  abx provider run api-key.resolve  [read]  Resolve an existing managed key without creating or renewing credentials.
  abx provider run api-key.update  [write]  Update an API key with secret values redacted.

  abx provider run quota.get  [read]  Get a Team resource quota.
  abx provider run quota.list  [read]  List one page of Team resource quotas.
  abx provider run quota.update  [write]  Replace a Team CPU and memory quota, including zero limits.

  abx provider run snapshot.delete  [delete]  Delete a Snapshot UUID independently of its source sandbox.
  abx provider run snapshot.list  [read]  List one Snapshot page, optionally filtered by source sandbox or name.
  abx provider run snapshot.restore  [write]  Create a new sandbox from a Snapshot UUID.
  abx provider run team.create  [write]  Create a Team.
  abx provider run team.delete  [delete]  Delete a Team.
  abx provider run team.get  [read]  Get a Team.
  abx provider run team.list  [read]  List one page of Teams.
  abx provider run team.update  [write]  Update a Team.
  abx provider run template-cache.create  [write]  Submit an explicit Team/template image-cache request; inspect status before reporting ready.
  abx provider run template-cache.delete  [delete]  Delete an explicit Team/template cache; underlying template is retained.
  abx provider run template-cache.get  [read]  Get actual Template Cache status, progress and image size.
  abx provider run template-cache.list  [read]  List one Team-scoped Template Cache page; return the opaque next token.
  abx provider run template.create  [write]  Register a native template from an image or build steps; rejects existing names. Submission does not mean ready. Use --input-file for private registry credentials.
  abx provider run template.delete  [delete]  Delete the selected Team's native cloud template; Sandbox instances are separate resources.
  abx provider run template.get  [read]  Read a native cloud template and its actual build status.
  abx provider run template.list  [read]  List native cloud templates in the configured Team (or the first Team returned for the same AK/SK) (all pages).
  abx provider run volume.create  [write]  Create a Volume mount configuration.
  abx provider run volume.delete  [delete]  Delete Volume metadata; underlying storage is retained.

  abx provider run volume.list  [read]  List one page of Volumes.
  abx provider run volume.update  [write]  Update Volume status.

### sandbox --help

```
$ abx sandbox --help
Invoke an operation declared by a Sandbox's bound OpenAPI contract.

Usage: abx sandbox TARGET [OPERATION] [options]

  abx sandbox TARGET --bind ./registry.yaml
  abx sandbox TARGET --help
  abx sandbox TARGET OPERATION --help
  abx sandbox TARGET OPERATION --body @request.json

TARGET is an existing Sandbox ID or local Sandbox deployment name.
Help is offline. Invocation never creates a Sandbox or falls back to shell execution.

Options:
  --help, -h                 Show the target's operations or an operation's contract
  --api NAME                 Select an API when operation IDs are ambiguous
  --body JSON|@FILE          JSON request body (maximum 1 MiB)
  --path NAME=VALUE          Path parameter; repeat for multiple parameters
  --query NAME=VALUE         Query parameter; repeat for multiple parameters
  --header NAME=VALUE        Declared non-authentication header parameter
  --timeout SECONDS          HTTP request deadline, default 30; maximum 300
  --bind FILE                Bind a local registry.yaml to this actual Sandbox
  --resource sandbox.NAME    Select one resource when the registry declares several
  --credential API.SCHEME=SOURCE
                             Explicit source: env:VARIABLE or config:server_token
  --alias NAME=API:OPERATION  Local operation alias; repeat as needed

Binding replaces this target's saved contract, credentials references and aliases.
Use global --provider before sandbox to select a Provider. Platform commands such
as abx exec, files, status and delete remain separate from application operations.
Exit code: 0
```

### exec --help

```
$ abx exec --help
Usage: abx exec [options] <SANDBOX_ID> <COMMAND...>

Run a command in a sandbox and preserve its exit code.

Everything after the sandbox ID is passed through to the remote command.
Put abx options before the ID. A single quoted argument is a shell command
line; several arguments are shell-quoted individually.

Express forwards piped stdin and EOF when supported by the sandbox.
--background prints the process ID and returns; --json returns structured
stdout, stderr and exit_code without mixing terminal output into JSON.

Examples:
  abx exec abc123 python --version
  abx exec --cwd /app --timeout 300 abc123 pytest -q
  abx exec --env DEBUG=1 abc123 python app.py
  abx exec --background abc123 python -m http.server 8000
  abx --json exec abc123 echo ready

Options:
  -c, --cwd <CWD>          Working directory (empty = container default)
  -u, --user <USER>        Run as the specified sandbox user
  -e, --env <ENV>          Environment variable for the command, format
                           KEY=VALUE (repeatable)
  -t, --timeout <INTEGER>  Command deadline in seconds (Express: no deadline;
                           other Providers: 60s)
  --background             Start the command, print its pid after piped stdin
                           reaches EOF; do not wait for remote completion
  --stream                 Print stdout/stderr live while the command runs
  -v, --verbose            Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -h, --help               Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### connect --help

```
$ abx connect --help
Usage: abx connect [options] <SANDBOX_ID>

Open an interactive sandbox terminal.

Express uses a PTY: shell state, terminal resizing and control characters
are preserved. Other Providers use the existing line-based command REPL;
each line runs in its own process. Use exec for automation.

Examples:

  abx connect --cwd /app --user root abc123

Options:

Exit code: 0

### provider install --help

```
$ abx provider install --help
Usage: abx provider install [options] <SOURCE>

Install a provider plugin from a directory or a git URL.

SOURCE is a local directory, owner/repo//subdir[@ref] (same // as
'abx template init --from'), or a git URL (https://, ssh://, git@host:path).
The plugin's abx-provider.toml is validated and its tree digest recorded.
After consent, default verification may load and initialize the plugin. A
consent screen
lists what the plugin runs, which features it provides and which generic
credentials it would receive. Non-interactive installs need --yes.
Progress and terminal elapsed time go to stderr; --json/--quiet suppress them.

A full 40-hex commit (--ref) or --sha256 pins the install. Tag and branch
installs are unpinned: they are accepted only after you read the consent
screen in a terminal (without --yes) or with --allow-unpinned; --yes alone
never accepts a moving ref.

Examples:
  abx provider install ./my-provider
  abx provider install ./my-provider --link --yes     # development: use in
place
  abx provider install alibaba-agent-sandbox/awesome-providers//opensandbox
  abx provider install https://github.com/acme/abx-provider-acme.git --ref
<commit>

Options:
  --ref <REF>                 Git tag, branch or commit (a full 40-hex commit
                              pins the install)
  --subdir <SUBDIR>           Plugin directory inside the repository
  --sha256 <SHA256>           Expected tree digest; the install fails if it
                              differs (pins the install)
  --link                      Link a local directory for development (no copy,
                              no integrity check; requires --yes; POSIX only)
  --force                     Replace an installed provider with the same id
  --allow-unpinned            Allow a tag/branch install without --sha256 in
                              non-interactive mode
  --allow-insecure-transport  Allow file://, git:// and http:// sources (testing
                              only)
  -y, --yes                   Skip the confirmation prompt (required in
                              non-interactive mode)
  -h, --help                  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### provider update --help

```
$ abx provider update --help
Usage: abx provider update [options] [ID]

Update installed providers from their recorded git source.

Without ID (or with --all) every git-installed provider is checked. A
pinned install stays put unless --ref names a new commit. --check only
reports what would change. Changes to runtime, security, features, config
fields or inherited credentials ask for consent again. A failed handshake
rolls back to the previous version (the data directory is preserved).
Directory and --link installs cannot be updated: reinstall with --force.
The bundled alicloud-express provider follows abx releases. Naming it
reports upgrade guidance, without replacing abx or checking host releases.

Options:
  --ref <REF>                 Git tag, branch or commit to update to
  --check                     Only report available updates
  --all                       Update every installed git provider
  --allow-unpinned            Allow an unpinned update in non-interactive mode
  --allow-insecure-transport  Allow file://, git:// and http:// sources (testing
                              only)
  -y, --yes                   Skip the confirmation prompt
  -h, --help                  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### template list --help

```
$ abx template list --help
Usage: abx template list [options] [QUERY]

Search the template catalog by name, tag, or description.

Queries the template index published in the
alibaba-agent-sandbox/awesome-templates
repository - the single source of truth for official and community
templates. The fetched index is cached under ~/.abx/index/ and reused for
up to an hour; on network failures the cached copy is served with a
warning.

For private mirrors / higher rate limits a token is taken from --token,
then the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, then ./.env, then the stored
github_token (in that order); prefer 'abx config set github_token'.

Examples:
  abx template list python
  abx template list ai-agent
  abx template list browser --status official
  abx template list qwen --tag deploy
  abx template list python --refresh    # bypass the local cache

Related commands:
  abx template init --from <name>             Install a template by index name
  abx template init --from owner/repo//subdir[@ref]
  abx template list

Options:
  -t, --tag <TAG>          Filter by exact tag name
  -s, --status <STATUS>    Filter by template status (choices: "official",
                           "community", "experimental")
  --index-url <INDEX_URL>  Template index location: HTTP(S) URL or local file
                           path (env: ABX_TEMPLATE_INDEX_URL; default: the
                           canonical remote index)
  --token <TOKEN>          GitHub token for private repos / higher rate limits.
                           Prefer 'abx config set github_token' (masked input,
                           stored once in ~/.abx/.env); --token is a temporary
                           override that may leak into shell history and the
                           process list (env: GITHUB_TOKEN).
  --refresh                Force a re-fetch of the index, ignoring the local
                           cache
  -h, --help               Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0

### template init --help

```
$ abx template init --help
Usage: abx template init [options] [DIRECTORY]

Scaffold a new sandbox template project.

Creates a ready-to-build template directory with template.yaml,
Dockerfile, and (depending on the case) a commands.py file.
Nothing is built, pushed, deployed, or turned into a sandbox.

When DIRECTORY is omitted a new ./<name> subdirectory is created
(derived from --name, the scaffold case, or the fetched template).
Existing nonempty directories show the affected entries before writing.
Interactive replacement requires confirmation; in scripts use --force
explicitly. --yes alone never authorizes overwriting existing entries.

--prompt requests natural-language template generation; DIRECTORY always
names a directory. Template generation (Qwen Code, needs 'abx config init
--llm')
writes Dockerfile, commands.py (the HTTP server) and template.yaml into
./<name>/ and stops. An interactive
terminal is asked for that directory first (Enter keeps ./<name>/).
A path token (my-app, ./my app) stays a directory.

--adopt adapts a project that already has source code and no template
files. Template generation sees a copy, and only Dockerfile, commands.py,
template.yaml and a generated .dockerignore are written back, after you
confirm. Nothing is built or deployed.

Examples:
  abx template init --list                     # List built-in cases
  abx template init -t python                  # Creates ./python/
  abx template init -t python --name myapp     # Creates ./myapp/
  abx template init -t python ./my-template    # Explicit directory
  abx template init --from owner/repo          # Creates ./<template-name>/
  abx template init --prompt "a python data science env"  # generate files only,
no build
  abx template init -y --prompt "a node.js api server"    # non-interactive
generation
  abx template init --adopt . --hint "port 8080" # adapt this project
  abx template init --adopt ./app --dry-run      # show what would be sent

Related commands:
  abx template build DIRECTORY
  abx deploy DIRECTORY --name my-app
  abx template publish DIRECTORY --tag VERSION

Options:
  --prompt <PROMPT>                Generate a template from a natural-language
                                   description
  -t, --template <CASE>            Built-in scaffold case (python, node,
                                   minimal, mcp)
  --from <FROM_REF>                Fetch template source from a registry ref
                                   (owner/repo, local path)
  --token <TOKEN>                  GitHub token for private repos / higher rate
                                   limits. Prefer 'abx config set github_token'
                                   (masked input, stored once in ~/.abx/.env);
                                   --token is a temporary override that may leak
                                   into shell history and the process list (env:
                                   GITHUB_TOKEN).
  --registry-url <REGISTRY_URL>    Source registry URL for --from
  --registry-type <REGISTRY_TYPE>  Source registry type for --from (choices:
                                   "github", "local")
  --name <NAME>                    Template name (default: case name, or fetched
                                   template name)
  --list                           List available scaffold cases
  --force                          Overwrite existing files
  --adopt                          Adapt an existing source project: template
                                   generation adds the template files
                                   (Dockerfile, commands.py, template.yaml).
                                   DIRECTORY is the project (default: .).
  --hint <HINT>                    With --adopt: what the code cannot tell the
                                   generator (ports, services).
  --dry-run                        With --adopt: list what would be sent to the
                                   model. Nothing is sent or written.
  -v, --verbose                    Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -y, --yes                        Skip confirmation prompts: the template
                                   directory, description clarification, and
                                   (with --adopt) the send and write prompts.
                                   Required for non-interactive template
                                   generation. Does not build or deploy.
                                   Replacing an existing Dockerfile still needs
                                   --force when there is no interactive preview.
  --model <MODEL>                  Model id for natural-language generation.
                                   Overrides llm_model for this command. An
                                   interactive terminal offers coding and chat
                                   models with the arrow keys when the chosen id
                                   does not exist.
  -h, --help                       Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### config init --help

```
$ abx config init --help
Usage: abx config init [options]

Guided setup with optional template search and launch (add --build / --llm for
focused setup).

Choose an existing Sandbox API key, or skip it to configure AK/SK.
Managed keys need Team-scoped CreateApiKey, DescribeApiKey and UpdateApiKey.
Creating or renewing a key requires confirmation (automation: provider run
api-key.prepare --yes).
Setup only saves configuration; it never creates a key. Secrets are masked
and stored in ~/.abx/.env; the region goes to ~/.abx/config.toml.

``--build`` adds the template build & push settings: the ACR namespace
and the Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pair (needed by ``abx template
build`` and ``abx deploy``).

``--llm`` adds the LLM API key used for template generation
(``abx template init --prompt "<description>"``).

After basic setup, choose Find and launch a template to search the
catalog and create without leaving the wizard. Missing build values
are collected by the same configuration prompts. An application token
is generated and saved for deployment; API bindings can select
config:server_token.

In non-TTY environments (CI, piped input) the wizard never blocks: it
prints the equivalent non-interactive ``abx config set ...`` commands
and exits successfully. ``--yes`` behaves the same way.

Examples:
  abx config init                 # credentials + region
  abx config init --build         # ... plus ACR namespace and AccessKey
  abx config init --llm           # ... plus the LLM API key
  abx config init --yes           # print non-interactive commands

Related commands:
  abx config list           Review effective values and sources
  abx config set KEY VALUE  Set one value directly
  abx config set KEY ""     Clear one stored value

Options:
  -y, --yes   Non-interactive: print the equivalent commands instead of
              prompting
  --build     Also ask for the selected provider build settings
  --llm       Also ask for the LLM API key used for template generation
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### config set --help

```
$ abx config set --help
Usage: abx config set [options] <KEY> [VALUE]

Set a configuration value: KEY [VALUE].

Settings are stored in ~/.abx/config.toml, except credentials
(sandbox_api_key, access_key_id, access_key_secret, acr_namespace,
llm_api_key, github_token, server_token) which are
written to ~/.abx/.env using their environment-variable names. Setting
llm_api_key is stored in ~/.abx/.env (the secret
migrates to the 0600-protected ~/.abx/.env storage).

Passing an empty VALUE clears the stored value for KEY instead: the key
falls back to its built-in default or becomes not set. An empty string
is never stored as a credential or override. Environment variables that
are still exported keep overriding the key at runtime; their values are
never printed. Clearing llm_api_key removes both the ~/.abx/.env entry

In an interactive terminal VALUE may be omitted: sensitive keys
(github_token, sandbox_api_key, access_key_secret, llm_api_key, server_token)
are then
read through the masked (asterisk) input and the typed value is never
echoed; other keys use a visible prompt. Pressing Enter at the prompt
cancels without changing anything. In CI / non-interactive sessions
VALUE is required.

Available keys (expected value):
  sandbox_api_key    Sandbox service API key (string; env var
                     ABX_SANDBOX_API_KEY).
                     ``api_key`` is accepted as an alias.
  access_key_id      Alibaba Cloud AccessKey ID for AK/SK auth, used by
                     managed keys, template deploy and ACR push (string)
  access_key_secret  Alibaba Cloud AccessKey Secret for AK/SK auth, used by
                     managed keys, template deploy and ACR push (string)
  acr_namespace      ACR namespace for template build, push, and install
                     (string; stored in ~/.abx/.env as ACR_NAMESPACE)
  api_url            Platform API URL (e.g.
https://api.cn-hangzhou.e2b.fc.aliyuncs.com)
  domain             Envd data-plane domain (e.g.
cn-hangzhou.e2b.fc.aliyuncs.com)
  region             Default region (e.g. cn-hangzhou, cn-shanghai)
  http_timeout       HTTP request timeout in seconds (number, e.g. 120)
  http2              Enable HTTP/2 (true/false)
  llm_api_key        LLM API key for template generation,
                     e.g. a DashScope/ModelStudio key (string; stored in
                     ~/.abx/.env as ABX_LLM_API_KEY)
  llm_model          LLM model name (default: qwen3-coder-plus)
  llm_base_url       LLM API base URL, OpenAI-compatible (string;
                     default: DashScope compatible-mode)
  github_token       GitHub token for template downloads, used by
                     'abx template init --from' / 'abx template list'
                     (string; stored in ~/.abx/.env)

Examples:
  abx config set sandbox_api_key YOUR_API_KEY
  abx config set access_key_id YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  abx config set access_key_secret YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  abx config set acr_namespace YOUR_ACR_NAMESPACE
  abx config set region cn-hangzhou
  abx config set http_timeout 120
  abx config set http2 false
  abx config set llm_api_key YOUR_DASHSCOPE_OR_LLM_KEY
  abx config set region ""          # clear the stored region
  abx config set sandbox_api_key ""  # remove the stored sandbox API key
  abx config set github_token      # masked prompt (VALUE omitted)
  abx config set github_token YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN
  abx config set github_token ""    # remove the stored token

Related commands:
  abx config get KEY       Verify the effective value
  abx config list          Review effective values and sources
  abx config delete KEY    Remove one stored value

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### config list --help

```
$ abx config list --help
Usage: abx config list [options]

List all effective configuration values and their sources.

Values are grouped by function — Sandbox authentication, Alibaba
Cloud credentials, connection, LLM and integrations —
in a stable order. Group titles are
display-only: ``config get`` and ``config set`` keep taking the bare
key names, and ``--json`` output stays a flat ``{key: value}`` map.

Sources: ``(env)`` a process environment variable, ``(user)`` a value
in ``./.env`` or stored with ``abx config set``, ``(default)`` a
built-in default, and ``(not set)`` when no value exists anywhere.
A set environment variable wins over either file. ``./.env`` wins
over ``~/.abx`` for a key it sets; a key it omits still comes from
``~/.abx``. Sensitive values are always masked.

Examples:
  abx config list
  abx --json config list
  abx config get http_timeout

Related commands:
  abx config get KEY        Inspect one effective value
  abx config set KEY VALUE
  abx config delete KEY     Remove one stored value

Options:
  --all       Also list provider keys that have no value
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### mcp start --help

```
$ abx mcp start --help
Usage: abx mcp start [options]

Start the MCP server and print its configuration to stderr.

The default transport is STDIO: an IDE writes JSON-RPC to stdin and reads
responses from stdout. Run it in a terminal to see the configuration and
stop it with Ctrl-C or 'abx mcp stop'.

--http listens for Streamable HTTP. --background detaches that HTTP
server; STDIO cannot keep a client attached after detach, so --background
starts HTTP.

Examples:
  abx mcp start
  abx mcp start --template python-hello
  abx mcp start --http --port 9000
  abx mcp start --http --background
  abx mcp stop

Related commands:
  abx mcp install --target cursor  Register the STDIO command in an IDE
  abx mcp stop                     Stop the local MCP server
  abx mcp status                   Check authentication and IDE setup

Options:
  --template <TEMPLATE>      Default sandbox template ID or alias (default:
                             code-interpreter-v1).
  --api-key <API_KEY>        API key override.
  --api-url <API_URL>        API URL override.
  --domain <DOMAIN>          Domain override.
  --http                     Serve Streamable HTTP instead of STDIO.
  --host <HOST>              HTTP bind address. [default: 127.0.0.1]
  --port <INTEGER>           HTTP bind port. [default: 9000]
  --auth-token <AUTH_TOKEN>  Bearer token for the HTTP server. Required when
                             --host is not loopback.
  --background               Detach an HTTP server. Stop it later with 'abx mcp
                             stop'.
  -h, --help                 Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```
